content:
maria: FYI nightly-eval 2025-10-12 03:00 UTC showed a clear drop after promptset_v5 landed on the quantized 3b build. negation bucket worst hit.

sam: how bad? paste the numbers? :grimacing:

maria: overall delta -0.058 relative. negation went 0.79 -> 0.60, numeric_precision 0.91 -> 0.86. failing examples 31/200. eval-bot attached the diff and examples.

eval-bot: nightly-eval summary
- model: rwd-open-3b-quant
- promptset: promptset_v5 (post-rebaseline)
- metrics: {"overall": -0.058, "negation": -0.19, "numeric_precision": -0.05}
- failing_examples_count: 31

anita: did the rebaseline change how we phrase negatives? sometimes compressing variants can remove helpful cues for smaller models.

maria: yes. PR consolidated several negative-phrasing variants into one lean template. example snippet from the change: 
``
- Prompt: "If that's NOT true, reply "false"."
- Prompt: "When it's incorrect, answer no."
+ Prompt: "If the statement is false, respond "false"."
```
My hypothesis: rwd-open-3b-quant relied on the verbose forms to resolve double-negatives.

lee: makes sense. compressed language reduces explicit tokens that hint at negation structure. small/quant models are brittle to that.

derek: can we isolate by running the exact failing examples with v4 vs v5 phrasing? if local reproduce, we'll know it's the prompt change.

maria: ran a focused eval: `pytest tests/evals/test_negation_variants.py::test_v5_vs_v4 -q` and it reproduces; v5 loses majority of the negation cases.

sam: remediation options? full revert of rebaseline, partial rollback, or augment with targeted variants?

anita: propose targeted restore: reintroduce the most diagnostic verbose negative variants only for the negation group, mark as canary so we don't affect unrelated buckets. less blast radius.

lee: +1. add flags in the promptset registry so the canary applies to a subset of eval traffic.

maria: opening PR rwd/promptsets#8492 — adds two verbose negative variants back into promptset_v5 under `negation_canary` and sets `canary:true` for the register entry. PR includes failing_examples.txt and eval logs.

sam: I'll review. need one eng-ml + one QA quick approve to fast-track.

anita: taking QA. checklist: run local focused eval, generate 10 sample outputs for the modified prompts, verify no regression in other metric buckets (fluency/hallucination/length).

derek: also add the exact generation seeds and model-config to the PR so others can reproduce.

maria: PR updated with seeds, config, and a short script `tools/repro/repro_negation.sh`. also linked nightly run.

sam: approved. :thumbsup:

anita: QA approved after running the checklist. numeric_precision unchanged. no regressions in hallucination or fluency.

deploy-bot: started canary deploy for promptset_v5 (negation_canary) -> 10% eval traffic

maria: halfway through canary: negation metric for canary slice climbing back to ~0.74. overall delta narrowing.

lee: that's promising. keep monitoring numeric_precision but seems orthogonal. maybe quant rounding interacts with numerics; file a follow-up.

maria: created an internal ticket INF-2745 to explore quantization rounding noise on numeric outputs. added logs and sample diffs.

sam: once canary passes 2h sweep, merge patch permanently and cut a micro release of prompt registry. also add a checklist item to rebaseline PRs.

derek: added a line to the rebaseline PR template: run targeted `eval:negation` and `eval:numeric` before merging rebaseline changes that compress phrasing.

maria: PR merged after canary. micro-release 0.5.1 of promptset registry published. tagging folks: @sam @anita @lee @derek.

sam: filing a short incident note in #postmortems with links to PR, nightly run, and follow-up ticket.

maria: resolved for now. will re-open thread if nightly re-trips.
